Kuvitus: suunnistuskartta kivellä kuusim: Illustration: an orienteering map on a rock in a spruce forest. A compass lies on the map, and beside it a bar magnet with its reddish and blue ends visible. The compass needle has turned towards the magnet and does not point in the direction of the north arrow of the map.
Periaatekuva sauvamagneetin magneettiken: Schematic figure of the magnetic field of a bar magnet seen from above. Green field lines start from the north pole N of the magnet, curve round the magnet and return to the south pole S; inside the magnet the lines continue from the south pole to the north pole, so each line is a closed loop. Arrowheads show the direction of the field. Four compasses around the magnet turn to point along the field lines: the north end of a compass points in the direction of the field. The lines are densest at the poles, so the field is strongest there.
Periaatekuva: sauvamagneetti katkaistaan: Schematic figure: a bar magnet is cut first in two and then into four pieces. Each piece still has both a north pole N and a south pole S in the same order as in the original magnet. No separate single pole appears.
Periaatekuva, ei mittakaavassa: rautakap: Schematic figure, not to scale: the magnetic domains of a piece of iron. On the left is unmagnetised iron whose domains have magnetic directions, the white arrows, pointing in different directions, so their effects cancel. On the right a magnet has been brought next to the piece of iron, north pole N first. The field of the magnet turns the domains and makes those along the field grow, so almost all the arrows point away from the magnet. The iron has become magnetised: its end nearest the magnet is a south pole S, and the magnet attracts it.
Periaatekuva, ei mittakaavassa: Maa ja s: Schematic figure, not to scale: the Earth and its magnetic field. Inside the Earth is drawn an imaginary bar magnet tilted about ten degrees from the axis of rotation. Its south pole S is near the geographic North Pole and its north pole N near the geographic South Pole. Green field lines start from the southern hemisphere and curve through space to the northern hemisphere. A compass in the northern hemisphere points north, and the lines dip steeply into the ground there.
Kaavakuva mittakaavassa, ylhäältä nähtyn: Formula figure to scale, seen from above: at the compass the horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field B_h = 14 µT points north, that is upwards, and the field of the magnet B_m = 20 µT points east, that is to the right, towards the south pole S of the magnet on the right. The sum B of the fields is the diagonal of a rectangle, and the compass needle turns to point along it by an angle θ from north towards east.
Kaavakuva mittakaavassa, sivulta nähtynä: Formula figure to scale, seen from the side: in southern Finland the Earth's magnetic field B = 52 µT points north and 74 degrees below the horizontal. The horizontal component B_h of the field is about 14 µT and the vertical component B_v about 50 µT. A compass turns only according to the horizontal component.
Kuvitus: jääkaapin ovi, jossa magneetit: Illustration: a fridge door where magnets hold a child's drawing and a shopping list. The steel sheet of the door attracts the magnets.
Periaatekuva: kaksi merkitsemätöntä harm: Schematic figure: two unlabelled grey bar magnets on the same line, end to end, with a gap between them. Green field lines start from the ends of both magnets next to the gap, curve away from each other upwards and downwards, and do not run from one magnet to the other. At the middle of the gap there is a point through which no line passes. The lines have no direction arrows.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa, ylhäältä nähtynä:: Graph to scale, seen from above: a grid square is 5 µT. Two green arrows start from the compass, the origin of the grid. The arrow B_h points north, that is upwards, and the arrow B_m east, that is to the right. The length of an arrow shows the magnitude of the field in microtesla on the scale of the grid. The total field, the compass needle and the angle are not drawn.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa, sivulta nähtynä:: Graph to scale, seen from the side: the horizontal ground and a grid whose square is 5 µT. The horizontal axis is towards the north and the vertical axis downwards. One green arrow B starts from the origin on the ground and points obliquely down towards the north. The tip of the arrow is at a point of the grid whose values the reader reads from the grid. The components and the angle are not drawn.
